I have been farming this same land for 35 years. My mother farmed it before me. I know this soil. I know what works.

All 5 mu go into the rotation — wheat in winter, maize in summer. Same land, same cycle, every year. I have no reason to change this. My neighbors do the same. The cooperative buys both crops at stable prices.

**For wheat:** I will rotary till after the maize comes off in September. The straw from maize, I will chop and leave in the field — it saves me buying so much fertilizer. I will plant improved wheat seed. I have been buying the same variety from the township supply station for four years now. It does not lodge, the heads are full, and I know what yield to expect. I apply compound fertilizer before planting, then go back with urea at jointing in April. I water three times: once before planting if the ground is dry, once in late winter to protect the roots from freezing, once at jointing. I spray herbicide in March when the weeds come up, and watch for aphids near heading — if I see them, I spray once more. My wheat gives me around 480 jin per mu most years.

**For maize:** The day after wheat harvest, I plant maize. No tillage — there is no time and the soil is already worked. I buy hybrid seed every year. I do not save seed for maize — the hybrid gives much better ears. I put compound fertilizer in at planting. When the maize reaches my knee, I scatter urea between the rows. I water at planting to get germination and once more at silking if the sky does not help me. Two people, 5 mu — I can manage this. I check for corn borer; if I find it, I spray once.
